chunks: Fadalah ibn Sinan, from al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan, from 'Ajlān Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said:

Treat people fairly with yourself, assist them with your wealth, and be pleased for them with what you are pleased for yourself. Remember Allah often, and beware of laziness and ennui, for that is what my father used to advise me, and that is what his father would advise him, and that applies to the night prayer. Indeed, if you are lazy, you will not fulfill the right of Allah, and if you are lethargic, you will not fulfill anyone else's right.

key_terms.أَنْصِفِ النَّاسَ مِنْ نَفْسِكَ: Treat people fairly with yourself (give them the same consideration you give yourself)
key_terms.وَاسِمْهُمْ مِنْ مَالِكَ: Assist/share with them from your wealth

ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical and spiritual qualities recommended for fulfilling one's duties to Allah and others?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines the spiritual prerequisites for valid night prayer (Salat al-Layl), linking the internal states of laziness (kasl) and ennui (dajjar) directly to the fulfillment of divine and human rights. This teaching, transmitted through the chain of Fadala ibn Qays, underscores the Shia emphasis on purifying the heart from spiritual lethargy to ensure the sincerity and completeness of worship.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 20.Faḍālah narrated from Qays al-Hilālī, from ʿAjlān Abū Ṣāliḥ who said, “Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) said, ‘

Treat people with fairness, assist them with your wealth, and wish for them what you wish for yourself. Remember Allah often and beware of laziness and ennui, for that's what my father used to advise me, and that is what his father would advise him, and it pertains [even more so] to the nightly prayer. Indeed if you are lazy, you will not fulfill the right of Allah and if you are lethargic, you will not fulfill anyone else’s right.’”
